problem_statement:
When debugging multithreaded applications, there is no way to determine which thread produced a given log message. The current logging subsystem does not support including thread identification in log output.

For applications with APIs callable from multiple threads, knowing the originating thread is essential for debugging. For example, a Bluetooth stack may have separate RX, TX, and main threads all logging through the same module — without thread context, correlating log messages to execution flow is impossible.

The logging subsystem needs:
1. A Kconfig option (CONFIG_LOG_THREAD_ID_PREFIX) to enable thread ID storage in log messages
2. The log message structure must be extended to carry the thread ID (tid) of the calling thread
3. The log output formatting layer must support rendering the thread ID prefix
4. When CONFIG_THREAD_NAME is also enabled, the thread name should be shown instead of a raw pointer

Expected output format with the feature enabled:
  <err> [main] module: Error message
  <inf> [sysworkq] bt_hci_core: TX process start
  <dbg> [BT RX] bt_att: tx_meta_data_alloc: disabling timeout

The changes span the log message structure, the output formatting layer, and the backend standard header.

See: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/61410
